Examples: A distribution has a percentile25 of 25. The data shows a percentile25 of 12.5. The scores have a percentile25 of 70.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

chosen_property.label: hasHeadToHeadWith
chosen_property.definition: A team has a head-to-head record with another team.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation.

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: hasOfferCatalog
candidates.comment: An offer catalog relation between an organization, person, or service and an associated offer catalog. Also called offers catalog, catalog of offers, product catalog. Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."

candidates.label: hasDriveThroughService
candidates.comment: A drive-through service availability relation for a place, indicating whether it offers services accessible by driving through. Also called offers drive-through, drive-through available, drive-in service. Examples: "A restaurant has drive-through service.", "A testing facility has drive-through service.", "The bank has drive-through service for transactions."

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: coach
candidates.comment: A leadership relation between a sports team and the person who acts as its coach. Also called "team coach", "trainer", "manager". Examples: "Basketball team coach John Smith", "Soccer team coach Jane Doe".

candidates.label: hasAdultConsideration
candidates.comment: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. Also called adult-oriented, age-restricted, mature content, for adults only. Examples: "An offer has adult consideration for explicit content.", "A product is tagged with adult consideration.", "This item has adult consideration due to its theme."

candidates.label: hasMap
candidates.comment: A map relation between a place and its associated map or map URL. Also called map of, location map, geographical map. Examples: "A restaurant has a map of its location.", "The park has a map showing its trails.", "This place has a map URL."

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: hasDefinedTerm
candidates.comment: A term inclusion relation between a defined term set or taxon and one of its contained defined terms. Also called contains term, includes term, term within. Examples: "A medical glossary has a defined term for 'hypertension'.", "A taxonomy has a defined term for 'Homo sapiens'.", "The dictionary has a defined term for 'algorithm'."

candidates.label: playMode
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the supported gameplay modes for a video game or series, such as single-player, multi-player, or co-op. Also called game mode, player configuration, gameplay style. Examples: A video game has a play mode of 'SinglePlayer'. A video game has a play mode of 'MultiPlayer'. A video game has a play mode of 'CoOp'.

candidates.label: inPlaylist
candidates.comment: A playlist inclusion relation between a music recording and the music playlist it belongs to. Also called part of playlist, on playlist, playlist track. Examples: "A music recording is in a playlist titled 'Workout Mix'.", "The song is in a playlist.", "This recording belongs to a specific playlist.". Distinct from inAlbum, which refers to a music album.

candidates.label: game
candidates.comment: A game relation between a game server and the video game that is hosted and played on it. Also called: hosted game, server game, game played. Examples: "Minecraft Server" game "Minecraft", "World of Warcraft Realm" game "World of Warcraft", "CS:GO Server" game "Counter-Strike: Global Offensive".

candidates.label: actor
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) or event and a person or performing group who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actor is 'Tom Hanks'.", "A play's actor is 'The Ensemble Theatre'.", "An episode's actor is 'Jane Doe'." Distinct from actors, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.

candidates.label: numberOfPlayers
candidates.comment: The number of people who can play a game or video game series, often expressed as a minimum, maximum, or range. Also called player count, game capacity, participant number. Examples: "Board Game X numberOfPlayers '2-4'", "Video Game Y numberOfPlayers '1 (single-player)'", "Online Game Z numberOfPlayers '100 (max)'".

candidates.label: characterName
candidates.comment: A naming relation for a performance role, indicating the name of the character being played. Also called "role name", "played character", "fictional name". Examples: "Actor's performance role characterName 'Hamlet'", "Actress's performance role characterName 'Juliet'". Distinct from character, which refers to the fictional person itself, whereas characterName is the name of the character in a specific performance.

candidates.label: sport
candidates.comment: An identification of the type of sport associated with a sports event or organization. Also called "sport type", "athletic discipline", "game played". Examples: "The event's sport is Basketball", "The organization's sport is Soccer", "This competition features the sport of Gymnastics."

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.
